payload.title: What Are the Brazilian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s, often with a Brazilian-Australian partner or parent, planning either a wedding in Brazil or a Brazilian-style celebration at home, who want to know what each custom means (from the right-hand ring and chá de panela to padrinhos, bem-casados and the groom's tie), what happens in what order, and what marrying legally in Brazil involves for Australians.
payload.goal: Read the free Wedded Wonderland digital magazine (primary CTA); secondary, in-context invitation to speak with a Wedded Advisor placed straight after the legal section on marrying in Brazil.
payload.service_link: /magazine (primary, UTM-tagged); /wonderland-concierge (secondary, UTM-tagged, after the legal section)
payload.angle: Page-one listicles (and our own old page, titled 8 but slugged 6) repeat unsourced gold shoes, rainbow bridesmaids and a 'church wedding is a must' line, and say nothing about Australians marrying in Brazil. We follow a Brazilian wedding in order (engagement and the ring moving from the right hand to the left, chá de panela, padrinhos, civil and religious ceremony, Saint Anthony and the Festa Junina mock wedding, names in the dress, bem-casados and docinhos, the groom's tie, music and dance with UNESCO's Samba de Roda and Frevo only where linked to celebrations), every meaning sourced or labelled 'often told', note once that customs vary by region, faith and family, and add what an Australian couple needs: Smartraveller's 'exercise a high degree of caution' level for violent crime (no higher-level areas, updated 27 October 2026), visa before arrival, consular help from Brasília and São Paulo (Rio's honorary consulate does no notarial work), and civil registration at the cartório from official sources.
must_include: Exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways at the top.

10 customs plus the legal section from tradition_plan in wedding order, grouped 'Before the wedding and the ceremony' (batch A) and 'The celebration' (batch B), each with a sourced meaning; unsourced origins labelled 'often told' or left out. Portuguese terms with correct diacritics (noivado, aliança, chá de panela, padrinhos, cartório, Santo Antônio, Festa Junina, bem-casado, docinhos, Recôncavo).

One line that Brazil is large and diverse and customs vary by region, faith (Catholic, Protestant and evangelical, Afro-Brazilian religions, secular) and family; regional notes only where sourced. No stereotypes, no carnival clichés.

Legal section for Australians marrying in Brazil: habilitação at the cartório de registro civil from gov.br, CNJ or the Código Civil; documents, apostille and sworn translation only as official sources state; recognition in Australia via the register-at-home link; same-sex marriage only from an official source; 'check with the cartório and the embassy, including any fees' where unreadable; 'as at November 2026'; no implied help with paperwork.

Smartraveller: overall 'Exercise a high degree of caution' due to violent crime, no higher-level areas, updated 27 October 2026 (still current 3 November 2026); visa before arrival; insurance covering medical evacuation; wet season by region and May to September wildfires for outdoor dates; drink spiking and methanol (branded, sealed drinks); yellow fever certificate may be needed; dual nationals enter on a Brazilian passport, possible military service for male dual nationals; same-sex relationships legal but not always accepted; avoid protests (inauguration in Brasília 5 January 2027); suggest places outside the western and northern border states Smartraveller names; prompt to check Smartraveller before booking.
Consular: Australian Embassy Brasília and Consulate-General São Paulo; Honorary Consulate Rio de Janeiro limited services and no notarial services.

Internal links: pillar /expert-advice/wedding-traditions in intro and close; /expert-advice/do-you-have-to-register-an-overseas-marriage-at-home from the legal section; /destinations/latin-america-caribbean (no Brazil hub in link map).

Short FAQ (5 to 6 questions) from SEO People Also Ask, sourced answers only; primary CTA /magazine, secondary Wedded Advisor CTA after the legal section; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions agreed in writing), never the 'first idea to the last dance' line.

tradition_plan.note: Planner fact-checks in 2 parallel batches with separate scratch folders (02-research/batch-a, 02-research/batch-b), 15 min HARD, save after every 3 facts, no extra sourcing rounds. Preferred sources: UNESCO ICH (ich.unesco.org), IPHAN (gov.br/iphan), gov.br, CNJ (cnj.jus.br), planalto.gov.br (Código Civil), Visit Brasil (visitbrasil.com), national museums, Britannica, academic sources; Portuguese dictionaries (Michaelis, Houaiss) for terms. Never competitor wedding sites or blogs as sole source. Smartraveller already fetched (02-research/pages/smartraveller.md); do not re-fetch. Old page notes in 02-research/pages/old-brazilian.md.
tradition_plan.count: 10 customs plus the legal section (6 in batch A, 3 customs plus legal in batch B)

batch_A.tradition: The engagement (noivado) and rings worn on the right hand, moved to the left at the wedding
facts_to_source: Engagement ring (aliança de noivado) worn on the right hand and moved to the left hand at the wedding: encyclopaedia, museum, academic or official tourism source; otherwise 'often told'
Couples often wearing matching bands (both partners) during the engagement: source or 'often told'
Portuguese terms noivado, noivos, aliança with diacritics as a dictionary prints them

batch_A.tradition: Chá de panela (kitchen shower) and similar showers
facts_to_source: What a chá de panela is (gifts for the couple's kitchen and home, hosted before the wedding) from a dictionary, encyclopaedia or academic source
Variants (chá de lingerie, chá bar or chá de casa nova) only if sourced; no gift values

batch_A.tradition: Padrinhos and madrinhas (wedding sponsors, often several couples)
facts_to_source: Role of padrinhos (witnesses and sponsors at the ceremony, often couples) from an encyclopaedic, academic or official source; number only if sourced
Civil witnesses (testemunhas) required at the civil marriage: number only from an official source (Código Civil or cartório guidance)
No claims about who pays for what

batch_A.kept_from_old_page: rewritten (old page said a church wedding is 'a must')
facts_to_source: Civil marriage before the cartório de registro civil as the legal act; religious marriage with civil effect (casamento religioso com efeito civil) only as the Código Civil, gov.br or CNJ states
Faith diversity (Catholic, Protestant and evangelical, Afro-Brazilian religions, secular): one line; any census figure only from IBGE with the year
No 'must have a church wedding' claim

batch_A.tradition: Saint Anthony (Santo Antônio) and the Festa Junina mock wedding
facts_to_source: Santo Antônio as the matchmaking saint (santo casamenteiro), feast day 13 June: encyclopaedia, IPHAN, Visit Brasil or academic source; any folk practices for finding a partner as 'often told'
Festas Juninas and the mock wedding (casamento caipira or casamento na roça) from IPHAN, Visit Brasil, encyclopaedia or academic source; no stereotyping of rural people
Any IPHAN registration of a São João celebration only if its page is confirmed live and the title matches

batch_A.tradition: The bride's name (or her single friends' names) written inside the dress or shoe
facts_to_source: Bride writing names of single friends inside the hem or sole, the one whose name wears off or stays said to marry next: source or 'often told' (no [[VERIFY]] if 'often told')
Drop gold shoes and the old page's framing

batch_B.kept_from_old_page: yes, re-sourced and rewritten (old page called it 'bomboniere')
facts_to_source: Bem-casado: two small sponge cakes joined with a filling (doce de leite or similar), wrapped and given to guests; name meaning 'well married'; good-luck meaning from an encyclopaedia, IPHAN, Visit Brasil or academic source, else 'often told'
Docinhos such as brigadeiros and beijinhos on the sweets table: what they are, sourced; no prices or vendor names
Neutral still-life AI image allowed only as illustrative pending approval

batch_B.tradition: The groom's tie cut and sold to guests
facts_to_source: Groom's tie cut into pieces and sold to guests to help the couple (gravata do noivo): source or 'often told'
Drop the old page's 'ceremonial' name for the reception and best-man auction detail unless sourced; no amounts

batch_B.tradition: Music and dance late into the night, with Samba de Roda and Frevo
facts_to_source: UNESCO: Samba de Roda of the Recôncavo of Bahia (proclaimed 2005, inscribed 2008) and Frevo, performing arts of the Carnival of Recife (2012); mention with weddings only where UNESCO's text links them to celebrations or festive occasions; otherwise present as music couples may choose
Long receptions and dancing late into the night: 'often told' unless sourced; no carnival clichés
No band or vendor names; regional music only where sourced

batch_B.tradition: Legal section: Australians marrying in Brazil
facts_to_source: Habilitação para o casamento at the cartório de registro civil: steps and documents from gov.br, CNJ or the Código Civil (Lei 10.406/2002); public notice (proclamas or edital) and validity period only as officially stated

Foreign nationals' documents: passport, birth certificate, proof of single status or certificate of no impediment, apostille (Brazil and Australia are Hague Apostille parties: source DFAT or gov.br), sworn translation by a tradutor juramentado: only as official sources state

Australian Embassy Brasília and Consulate-General São Paulo for consular help; the Honorary Consulate in Rio de Janeiro does not provide notarial services (Smartraveller, already fetched); certificate of no impediment process only from DFAT or the embassy

Same-sex marriage in Brazil only from an official source (e.g. CNJ Resolution 175/2013 if the page is read); Smartraveller says same-sex relationships legal but not always accepted, and does not mention marriage
Visa needed before arrival (Smartraveller); dual nationals enter on a Brazilian passport

Fees: 'a fee applies' only if an official source says so; otherwise 'check with the cartório and the embassy, including any fees'; 'as at November 2026'; [[VERIFY]] for anything unconfirmed; link /expert-advice/do-you-have-to-register-an-overseas-marriage-at-home

Brazilian-Australian community celebrations at home (only from a sourced community or museum page; no vendor names)

'Heel and toe dance' with money dropped into the bride's gold shoe: unsourced.
Reception called a 'ceremonial' and best man leading a tie 'auction' for the honeymoon: unsourced detail; tie custom kept only as sourced or 'often told'.
'Bomboniere' (Italian) for bem-casado, and 'bem casado' without hyphen.
Clichés and tone: 'colour, passion', 'extravagant weddings', 'exotic culture', 'gal pals', 'scissor action'; capitalised Wedding/Bride/Groom; typo 'extra crash'.
Images credited to Daniel Lateulade and cecinewyork.com with unconfirmed licences; unrelated Australian and Fiji venue and vendor widgets; Culture category; no brand terms, CTA or sources.

avoid: Reusing wording, structure, captions or images from the old page or any competitor.
Carnival clichés, stereotypes about Brazilians, favela imagery, 'passionate' or 'exotic' framing.
Presenting any custom as universal or tied to one faith without a source; 'ancient' or 'centuries-old' claims without a source.
Prices, fee figures, gift amounts, vendor or venue names.
Legal advice beyond official sources; never guess documents, fees, notice periods or waiting times; no implied help with legal paperwork.
UNESCO claims beyond Samba de Roda (2008) and Frevo (2012), and those only where the text links them to celebrations.
Headings with pasted keywords in brackets; em dashes; US spelling.

Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; the 'first idea to the last dance' line; AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places (AI only for a neutral still life of bem-casados, labelled illustrative pending approval).
